title.narrative: TerraMoldova: Expanding Sustainable Land and Biodiversity Management in Moldova

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The TerraMoldova project will generate tangible socioeconomic benefits for both national systems and local communities, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable regions. By restoring degraded ecosystems and integrating NBS into land management, the project will support resilient livelihoods, agricultural productivity, and long-term sustainability of natural capital.At the local level, the project directly benefits farmers, landowners, and local cooperatives by:? Enhancing soil fertility and water retention, critical for crop yields in erosion-prone and drought-affected areas.? Promoting biodiversity-friendly practices in viticulture and agroecosystems, opening access to green markets and boosting incomes.? Providing technical support and inputs to over 25 demonstration farms, fostering knowledge exchange and enabling replication.? Creating green jobs through field restoration, native plant propagation, and ecological monitoring, particularly benefiting youth and women through inclusive capacity-building programs.At the national level, the project strengthens Moldova’s institutional and legal architecture for ecological governance and supports implementation of the National Forest Extension and Rehabilitation Program (NFERP), Natura 2000 readiness, and Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) targets. These efforts align directly with GEF Trust Fund objectives by:? Mitigating GHG emissions through wetland rewetting, forest regeneration, and agroforestry, contributing to climate mitigation benefits.? Conserving and restoring habitats and species under the Global Biodiversity Framework, including Targets 2, 3, and 10.? Supporting cross-sectoral resilience and adaptation by reducing flood and drought risks in climate-sensitive zones.The project’s co-benefits include enhanced ecosystem service delivery (e.g., pollination, carbon sequestration, erosion control), improved agro-forest landscapes through eradicated IAS that harbors other invasives, and strengthened food and water security in vulnerable areas. Together, these outcomes advance Moldova’s contribution to global environmental benefits, while ensuring sustainable development dividends at home.
To increase the area under sustainable landscape management practices in targeted sites in Moldova
